title: Runtime Experimentation: Safety, Isolation, and Rollback Runbook
author: Priya Nambiar
content:
Summary
-------
This runbook defines the safety, isolation, rollout, and rollback procedures for running experiments that touch the serving runtime surface: kernel changes, scheduler policy updates, quantization rollouts, and affinity/topology experiments. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and experiment owners who run controlled experiments against live traffic.

Purpose and scope
-----------------
- Purpose: limit blast radius, provide deterministic rollback, and ensure experiment telemetry is sufficient to detect regressions to latency, error rate, and fidelity.
- Scope: changes to kernel selection, scheduling policy, K/V cache heuristics, admission controller parameters, runtime flags that alter execution fidelity.
- Exclusions: application-layer prompt tuning, customer prompt datasets, or non-runtime model artifacts (see product docs).

Owner and escalation
--------------------
- Runbook owner: Runtime Experiments Guild (oncall: runtime-experiments@redwood).
- Primary contacts: Priya Nambiar (runtime experiments lead), Ethan Brooks (SRE lead).
- Pager escalation: follow standard eng-sre incident process; if experiment causes SLA degradation escalate to Eng SRE oncall.

When to use this runbook
------------------------
Use this runbook for any runtime change that could impact per-token latency, tail latency, or model fidelity in production. Examples:
1) Kernel hint changes or new kernel rollout.
2) Scheduler credit/accounting policy adjustments.
3) Enabling a new prefetch/prefill strategy for KV cache.
4) Introducing a quantized-op fallback path.

Pre-flight checklist (must-pass before injecting traffic)
--------------------------------------------------------
1) Approval: experiment approved by a runtime owner and an SRE reviewer. Add approval comment to the experiment ticket.
2) Benchmarks: local and canary synthetic benchmarks executed; baseline and candidate run data attached to ticket.
3) Canary resources: dedicated canary pool provisioned (min 2 nodes/GPUs) and network isolation validated.
4) Observable hooks: dashboards, alerts, and traces created and reviewed. See Observability configuration section below.
5) Abort signals: a named alert and a quickstop playbook are configured (alerts must map to concrete thresholds).
6) Safety timeout: automatic experiment pause set to 60 minutes if manual approval not received.

Isolation matrix (traffic & environment)
---------------------------------------
| Experiment Type | Isolation step | Traffic fraction | Notes |
|-----------------|----------------|------------------|-------|
| Kernel rollout | Canary pool w/affinity | 1-5% | Ensure canary nodes are not used by customer-critical tenants |
| Scheduler policy | Simulated shadow + 0.5% live | 0.5-2% | Use shadow routing first then small live sample |
| KV cache heuristic | Shadow + canary | 1% | Measure hit/miss and warmup behavior |
| Quantized fallback | Offline validation + 0.5% | 0.5% | Validate fidelity using held-out prompts |

Observability configuration (required)
------------------------------------
- Dashboards: create or update a dashboard with the following panels: P50/P95/P99 latency, per-request kernel selection distribution, kernel queue depth, kernel preemption rate, KV cache hit rate, error rate (5xx + internal errors), model output fidelity metrics if applicable.
- Alerts (examples):
  - runtime.latency.p99 > 150ms over 5m for canary -> Severity: critical; automatic pause.
  - runtime.error.rate > 0.5% over 5m -> Severity: critical; automatic pause.
  - kernel.preemptions.per_min > 20 on any GPU -> Severity: warning.
  - kvcache.miss_rate.delta > 10pp vs baseline -> Severity: warning.
- Tracing: Ensure request traces sample rate >= 1% for experiment cohort and include kernel selection and scheduler decision tags.
- Logs: Enable DEBUG-level kernel-selection logs for canary nodes for the duration of the experiment (rotated out after collection).

Telemetry thresholds and automated stop conditions
--------------------------------------------------
- Hard stop (immediate rollback):
  - p99 latency increase > 40% relative to baseline for 5m window.
  - Total error rate > 1% for 5m.
  - Model fidelity regression: automatic detection based on eval prompts showing > 5% drop in correctness/score.
- Soft stop (pause and investigate):
  - p99 latency increase between 20% and 40% for 10m.
  - Error rate between 0.5% and 1% for 10m.
  - kvcache.miss_rate delta > 7pp.

Canary rollout sequence (recommended)
-----------------------------------
1) Offline lab validation: run candidate kernels or policy in lab with replay corpus. Record microbenchmarks and end-to-end latency traces.
2) Shadow experiment: enable shadow routing for 1–2 hours at production concurrency; collect traces and compare decisions.
3) Tiny live canary: route 0.5–1% live traffic to canary pool for 30–60 minutes. Check thresholds.
4) Small ramp: increase to 5% over 1–2 hours if metrics stable.
5) Progressive ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over multiple hours/days with manual gates between steps.
6) Full rollout: only after SRE signoff and 48h stable at 50%+.

Emergency rollback procedure (immediate actions)
------------------------------------------------
1) Hit hard-stop alert.
2) Execute immediate pause: set routing rule to revert canary/cohort to baseline model/kernels. Example command for routing service: 

```
# Revert canary cohort by name
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_API_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"cohort":"canary-123","action":"revert"}' \
  https://routing.internal.redwood/v1/cohorts/revert
```

3) Scale down canary pool to zero or detach nodes from serving plane. Example k8s label patch: 

```
kubectl label node gpu-canary-01 experiment=false --overwrite
kubectl cordon gpu-canary-01
kubectl drain gpu-canary-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

4) Notify oncall, SRE, and experiment owner via standard incident channel. Create incident ticket referencing experiment.
5) Preserve artifacts: collect traces, kernel logs, and profile dumps and attach to the incident.

Post-incident triage and artifact collection
-------------------------------------------
- Required artifacts to attach to postmortem:
  - Full dashboard snapshots for experiment window (timestamps).
  - Traces with kernel selection tags and sampled request payloads (redact PII).
  - Kernel profiles (nvprof/metrics) and occupancy reports.
  - Scheduler logs and admission controller events.
  - Repro corpus and steps used for offline replay.

Minimum artifact retention: keep all experiment-related artifacts for 90 days in the runtime experiments S3 bucket.

Observability onboarding template (checklist)
-------------------------------------------
- Panels to create: latency(p50/95/99), error rates per route, kernel-selection histogram, queue depth heatmap, per-GPU temperature and throttling, KV cache hit/miss and warmup curve.
- Alerts to wire: p99 latency, error rate, preemption spike, cache-miss delta.
- Traces: 1% sample for production, 5% for canary cohort.

Data privacy and compliance
--------------------------
- Do not store raw customer prompts or outputs in experiment buckets unless explicitly approved. Use anonymized or synthetic corpora for fidelity checks.
- If collecting traces that include request text, apply the redaction pipeline before long-term storage.

Troubleshooting common failure modes
----------------------------------
- Symptom: sudden p99 spike with no error-rate increase. Likely cause: kernel queueing or preemption.
  - Action: check kernel.queue_depth and kernel.preemptions. Reduce admission credits for the cohort.
- Symptom: fidelity regression on quantized path.
  - Action: enable shadow fallback to float path for the failing requests and collect diffs for top 50 prompts by frequency.
- Symptom: KV cache warmup causing high tail latency during rollout.
  - Action: increase warmup traffic, use traffic shaping or temporary routing to warm required prefixes.

Experiment audit & signoff
--------------------------
- All experiments must have a ticket with: hypothesis, metric targets, isolation plan, observability plan, rollback criteria, and owner.
- Signoff: runtime owner + SRE reviewer must explicitly approve before any live traffic changes. Approval should be recorded in the ticket.

Example YAML snippet: canary routing policy
-----------------------------------------
```yaml
apiVersion: routing.redwood/v1
kind: CanaryPolicy
metadata:
  name: canary-runtime-policy-2025-09
spec:
  cohort: canary-123
  initialFraction: 0.005
  steps:
    - wait: 30m
      fraction: 0.005
    - wait: 60m
      fraction: 0.05
    - wait: 120m
      fraction: 0.25
  healthChecks:
    - name: p99_latency
      threshold: 150 # ms
    - name: error_rate
      threshold: 0.005 # 0.5%
```

Appendix: quick diagnostic CLI commands
--------------------------------------
- Check canary p99 from metrics API:
```
curl -s "https://metrics.internal.redwood/api/query?expr=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{cohort=\"canary-123\"}[5m])) by (le))" | jq
```
- List kernel selection distribution from traces index:
```
curl -s "https://tracing.internal.redwood/api/traces?service=runtime&cohort=canary-123&limit=100" | jq '.[] | {trace_id:.id, kernel: .tags.kernel}'
```
